claim: A multi-objective reinforcement learning data scheduler that combines data quality, inter-domain influence, and model stability rewards achieves faster convergence to a given perplexity compared to static data mixing methods in LLM pre-training.
falsifier: The convergence benefit can be tested by comparing a multi-objective RL scheduler against static mixing or single-objective schedulers on different LLM architectures and datasets.

conditions: LLM pre-training on The Pile with Pythia-1B architecture
state representation includes sample counts and reward signals
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system (Pythia-1B on The Pile), scheduler design, and experimental conditions; transfer to other models or corpora is unestablished.

title: Multi-objective reinforcement learning scheduler for convergence speed
